title: Flood in Thailand
subtitle: reported 2026-11-05
association: The satellite flood maps are cut to the box around the outline that NASA EONET record EONET_26367 publishes for this event (source: GDACS). The product maps water wherever it is seen; water inside the box is not proof that it belongs to this event, and the reported outline is not a water edge. The reported start of the event is 2026-11-05; maps of earlier dates are shown for comparison.

summary.label: Mapped floodwater
summary.note: Pixels the NASA MODIS flood product classes as flood (water where its reference map has land) inside the box shown, on the map date named below (the largest value since the reported start). Clouds hide water, so this is a lower bound; the product can also mistake cloud or terrain shadow for water.

summary.label: Not observed
summary.note: Share of the box the product marks as insufficient data on that date: cloud, cloud or terrain shadow, and steep terrain that the product always masks.

summary.label: Spatial resolution
summary.note: One map per day, each made from 3 days of MODIS observations (Terra and Aqua), on the 250 m product grid.

steps_label: Flood map of the 3 days ending

source.name: NASA LANCE MODIS Near Real-Time Global Flood Product (MCDWD), 3-day composite, via NASA GIBS

layers.resolution: 250 m (0.0022° pixels, product grid, not resampled)
layers.units: class per pixel; areas in km²
layers.uncertainty: Cloud and terrain shadow can be mistaken for water or hide it; near-real-time product without field validation.
layers.note: Red = water where the product's reference water map has land. Yellow = places that flood regularly. Blue = normal water. Grey = not observed. No water depth is known.
